QuestionText: India's national sport is:
Options: A) Cricket
B) Kabaddi
C) Hockey
D) Badminton
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Field Hockey is India's national sport. India has won 8 Olympic gold medals in hockey (1928-1980) — the most by any country. The golden era: 1928-1956 when India won 6 consecutive Olympic gold medals, including the 1936 Berlin Olympics with Dhyan Chand (whose birthday, August 29, is celebrated as National Sports Day). India's recent revival: Bronze medals at Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Olympics. Dhyan Chand Award: highest sports honour for lifetime achievement in sports.

QuestionText: Who is known as the 'Flying Sikh' of India?
Options: A) Neeraj Chopra
B) Milkha Singh
C) P.T. Usha
D) Gurbachan Singh Randhawa
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Milkha Singh (1929-2021): legendary Indian sprinter — known as the 'Flying Sikh.' He won the 400m gold at 1958 Commonwealth Games and 1958 Asian Games. Heartbreaking near-miss: finished 4th in 400m final at 1960 Rome Olympics by 0.1 seconds (national record that stood for almost 40 years). Refused a Pakistani passport after the partition massacre that killed his family — an iconic moment in 1960 Pakistan race (broke the record while losing). Arjuna Award recipient. His life was depicted in the Bollywood film 'Bhaag Milkha Bhaag' (2013). Died during COVID-19 pandemic (2021).

QuestionText: Who is known as the 'Master Blaster' of cricket?
Options: A) Virat Kohli
B) MS Dhoni
C) Sachin Tendulkar
D) Sunil Gavaskar
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Sachin Tendulkar is called the 'Master Blaster' — widely regarded as cricket's greatest batsman. Records: First to score 100 international centuries (50 Tests + 49 ODIs), 15,921 Test runs, 18,426 ODI runs, most international runs (34,357). Played 1989-2013. Won ICC Cricket World Cup 2011 with India. Received Bharat Ratna (2014 — first sportsperson). Also received Padma Shri, Padma Vibhushan, Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna. Called 'God of Cricket' by Indian fans. Debut: 1989 at age 16 vs Pakistan. Retired from all cricket November 16, 2013.

QuestionText: Who won India's first individual Olympic gold medal?
Options: A) Leander Paes
B) Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore
C) Abhinav Bindra
D) P.V. Sindhu
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Abhinav Bindra won India's first individual Olympic gold medal in the 10m air rifle event at the 2008 Beijing Olympics. This was historic — India's only individual gold until Neeraj Chopra's javelin gold at Tokyo 2020. Bindra is a world-class shooter who also won World Championship gold in 2006. He received the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna (India's highest sports honour) and Padma Bhushan. Previously, India's Olympic gold medals were only in team hockey. India waited 60+ years for an individual Olympic gold after independence. Bindra's achievement inspired a generation of Indian shooters.

QuestionText: What is Bharatanatyam?
Options: A) A form of classical Indian wrestling
B) A classical Indian dance form originating in Tamil Nadu — one of India's oldest dance traditions
C) A classical Indian music style from Karnataka
D) A traditional Indian martial art
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Bharatanatyam: India's oldest classical dance form, originating in Tamil Nadu. Evolved from temple dances of devadasis (temple dancers). Named after Natya Shastra (Bharata Muni's ancient treatise on performing arts — 'Bharata'+'natya'). Characterized by: intricate footwork, expressive hand gestures (mudras), facial expressions (abhinaya), and sculpturesque poses. Major exponents: Rukmini Devi Arundale (revived it), Balasaraswathi, Mallika Sarabhai. India's 8 classical dance forms (Sangeet Natak Akademi recognized): Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Odissi, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Sattriya, Mohiniyattam.

QuestionText: What is the significance of Neeraj Chopra for Indian athletics?
Options: A) First Indian to compete in Olympics
B) First Indian to win Olympic gold in athletics (javelin, Tokyo 2020) — also won silver at Paris 2024
C) First Indian to run 100m in under 10 seconds
D) First Indian national cricket captain
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Neeraj Chopra: first Indian to win Olympic gold in a track and field event. Javelin gold at Tokyo 2020 Olympics (August 7, 2021) — threw 87.58m in finals. World's 2nd ranked javelin thrower. Silver at Paris 2024 Olympics (89.45m — personal best). World Athletics Championships 2023: Gold medal (88.17m) — first Indian to win world athletics championship gold. Also holds multiple Diamond League titles. Received Bharat Ratna nomination campaign. Born in Haryana — inspired thousands of javelin throwers. Padma Shri, Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna awardee. India's most decorated track and field athlete.

QuestionText: Who is P.V. Sindhu?
Options: A) India's top women's chess player
B) India's top women's badminton player — 2-time Olympic medallist (Silver-Rio 2016, Bronze-Tokyo 2020)
C) India's leading women's sprinter
D) A classical dancer who won Padma Bhushan
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: P.V. Sindhu (Pusarla Venkata Sindhu): India's top women's badminton player. Achievements: Silver medal at Rio 2016 Olympics, Bronze at Tokyo 2020 Olympics (2-time Olympic medallist), World Badminton Championship Gold (2019 — first Indian to win), multiple BWF World Championship medals (5 total — unprecedented by an Indian). At peak: ranked World No. 1. National coach: Pullela Gopichand (who also won All England Championship). Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna awardee. India's highest earning female athlete. Inspired a badminton revolution in India, especially in Hyderabad and Andhra Pradesh.

QuestionText: What is Rabindranath Tagore's significance in Indian culture?
Options: A) He composed India's national anthem 'Vande Mataram'
B) First Asian Nobel laureate — poet, philosopher, author of 'Jana Gana Mana' (national anthem) and 'Gitanjali'
C) He founded the Indian National Congress
D) He designed India's national flag
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Rabindranath Tagore (1861-1941): First Nobel laureate from Asia (Literature Nobel Prize 1913 for 'Gitanjali' — spiritual verse). Composed Jana Gana Mana (India's national anthem) and Amar Sonar Bangla (Bangladesh's national anthem) — only person to write national anthems of two countries. Founded Visva-Bharati University (Shantiniketan, West Bengal). Famous works: Gitanjali, Gora, Ghare Baire (The Home and the World), Rabindra Sangeet (famous musical compositions), paintings. Called 'Gurudev' (Divine Teacher) by Gandhi. Returned his knighthood after Jallianwala Bagh massacre. May 7 (his birthday) observed as Rabindra Jayanti.

QuestionText: What is Yoga and its global significance?
Options: A) A form of Indian wrestling
B) An ancient Indian physical, mental, and spiritual practice — UN declared June 21 as International Day of Yoga (2015) at India's initiative
C) A type of Indian folk dance
D) A meditation technique developed in modern times
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Yoga: originated in ancient India 5,000+ years ago. Practice combining: physical postures (asanas), breathing techniques (pranayama), meditation, and ethical principles. Multiple types: Hatha, Ashtanga, Vinyasa, Iyengar, Kundalini, Bikram, Restorative. UNESCO included Yoga in Intangible Cultural Heritage List (2016). International Day of Yoga (IDY): June 21 — declared by UN in December 2014 after India (PM Modi) proposed it. Celebrated globally with mass yoga sessions. India's Ministry of Ayush promotes yoga internationally. Patanjali's Yoga Sutras (~200 BCE): foundational text. Rishikesh (Uttarakhand) is the 'World Capital of Yoga.'

QuestionText: What are the major classical music traditions of India?
Options: A) Bollywood and folk music
B) Two main traditions: Hindustani (North India) and Carnatic (South India)
C) Four regional styles: Bengali, Marathi, Tamil, and Telugu
D) Classical Indian music has only one unified tradition
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Two classical music traditions: Hindustani (North Indian): influenced by Persian/Mughal music, more improvisation, ragas performed at specific times/seasons. Instruments: sitar, sarod, tabla, sarangi, bansuri. Maestros: Ravi Shankar, Bismillah Khan, Pandit Bhimsen Joshi. Carnatic (South Indian): older, more compositions (kritis), less improvisation, devotional basis. Instruments: veena, mridangam, violin (adapted), nadaswaram. Maestros: M.S. Subbulakshmi, Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer. Both use raga (melodic framework) and tala (rhythmic cycle) systems. Sangeet Natak Akademi promotes both traditions.

QuestionText: Who invented chess?
Options: A) Ancient Chinese civilization
B) Ancient India — chess (Chaturanga) was invented in India (Gupta period ~6th century CE)
C) Ancient Arabia
D) Ancient Greece
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Chess (Chaturanga): originated in India during the Gupta Empire (~6th century CE). Name 'Chaturanga' = four divisions (infantry, cavalry, elephants, chariots — represented by pawns, knights, bishops, rooks). Spread to Persia (Chatrang), then Arabia (Shatranj), then Europe (Chess). India's chess legacy continues: Viswanathan Anand — 5-time World Chess Champion (2000-2013) — India's most decorated individual sports champion and first non-European/non-Russian World Chess Champion. India currently dominates world chess: Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa reached World Chess Championship final (2023), and D. Gukesh became World Chess Champion in 2024 — youngest ever at 18.

QuestionText: What is the Kumbh Mela?
Options: A) A political gathering of Indian leaders
B) The world's largest peaceful gathering — Hindu pilgrimage held every 12 years at Prayagraj, Haridwar, Nashik, and Ujjain on a rotating basis
C) A traditional harvest festival of Maharashtra
D) A government-organized trade fair promoting Indian handicrafts
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Kumbh Mela: the world's largest human gathering — UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. Based on Hindu mythology — drops of amrit (nectar of immortality) fell at four locations: Prayagraj (Sangam — confluence of Ganga, Yamuna, Saraswati), Haridwar (Ganga), Nashik (Godavari), Ujjain (Shipra). Prayagraj's Maha Kumbh (every 12 years): 400-500 million visitors (2019 — world's largest gathering ever). Smaller Kumbhs (every 3 years): rotate between four cities. Ardh Kumbh (half): every 6 years at Prayagraj and Haridwar. Bathing in the river during auspicious dates (Shahi Snan) is the main ritual.

QuestionText: What is the significance of the Ajanta Caves?
Options: A) Fortress used by Marathas against Mughals
B) UNESCO World Heritage Buddhist rock-cut caves (Maharashtra) with ancient paintings and sculptures — considered among world's finest examples of Buddhist art
C) Ancient Hindu temples built by Pallava dynasty
D) Jain temples built in the Gupta period
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Ajanta Caves: 30 Buddhist rock-cut cave monuments in Aurangabad district, Maharashtra. Created in two phases: 2nd century BCE and 5th century CE (Vakataka period). UNESCO World Heritage Site (1983). Contains remarkable wall paintings and sculptures depicting Jataka stories (Buddha's past lives), Buddhist doctrines, and palace/court scenes. These are among the finest surviving examples of ancient Indian art. 'Lost' for centuries, rediscovered in 1819 by British officer John Smith during a tiger hunt. Ellora Caves (nearby): represents Buddhism, Hinduism, and Jainism in rock-cut monuments.

QuestionText: Who is M.S. Dhoni and what is his legacy in cricket?
Options: A) India's first cricket captain
B) India's most successful cricket captain — won ICC World T20 (2007), ICC World Cup (2011), ICC Champions Trophy (2013) — known as 'Captain Cool'
C) World's highest run-scorer in Test cricket
D) First Indian to score 100 international centuries
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Mahendra Singh Dhoni (MS Dhoni): arguably India's greatest cricket captain. Unique distinction of winning all three major ICC tournaments: ICC World T20 2007 (his first tournament as captain), ICC Cricket World Cup 2011 (India's home World Cup — Dhoni's iconic six to win the final), ICC Champions Trophy 2013. Known for: exceptional wicket-keeping, innovative batting (MS's helicopter shot), calm under pressure ('Captain Cool'). Retired from Test cricket (2014), ODI/T20I cricket (August 15, 2020). Led CSK (Chennai Super Kings) to 5 IPL titles. Born in Ranchi, Jharkhand — inspired cricket's expansion to smaller cities. Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna.

QuestionText: What is Diwali and its significance?
Options: A) Festival of colours
B) Festival of Lights — celebrates triumph of light over darkness, good over evil, knowledge over ignorance
C) India's harvest festival celebrated only in Punjab
D) A festival marking the beginning of the monsoon
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Diwali (Deepavali — row of lights): India's most widely celebrated festival. Date: Hindu calendar month of Kartik (October-November). Significance varies by tradition: North India — celebrates Lord Ram's return to Ayodhya after 14-year exile and victory over Ravana; South India — celebrates Krishna's victory over Narakasura; Jains — marks Mahavira's attainment of moksha; Sikhs — celebrates Guru Hargobind Singh's release from Mughal captivity. Celebrations: lighting of diyas (oil lamps) and candles, rangoli, fireworks (environmental concern), sweets exchange, new clothes, lakshmi puja (wealth goddess). Diwali is now celebrated globally by Indian diaspora.

QuestionText: Who is Viswanathan Anand?
Options: A) A legendary Indian classical musician
B) 5-time World Chess Champion — India's first world chess champion and most celebrated Indian individual sports champion
C) India's first Olympic gold medalist
D) A pioneer of Indian cinema
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Viswanathan Anand ('Vishy'): India's greatest chess player. 5-time World Chess Champion: 2000, 2007, 2008, 2010, 2012. First non-European/Russian to win World Chess Championship (2000). Rapid chess world champion. Known for: lightning-fast calculation, exceptional rapid/blitz chess skills. Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, Padma Vibhushan. Paved the way for India's current chess generation: Praggnanandhaa, Gukesh (2024 World Champion), Arjun Erigaisi, Nihal Sarin. India won Chess Olympiad 2024 gold in both Open and Women's sections — a historic achievement inspired by Anand's legacy.

QuestionText: What is the Taj Mahal and who built it?
Options: A) A Rajput fort in Jaipur
B) A white marble mausoleum in Agra built by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan (1632-1653) for his wife Mumtaz Mahal
C) A Buddhist stupa built by Emperor Ashoka
D) A palace built by Akbar for his wives
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Taj Mahal: built 1632-1653 by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal (who died in childbirth). Located in Agra, Uttar Pradesh. Made of white Makrana marble with intricate inlay work (pietra dura) using semi-precious stones. Symmetrical design with central dome (73m), four minarets, reflecting pool. UNESCO World Heritage Site (1983). One of Seven Wonders of the Modern World (voted 2007). Designed by architects including Ustad Ahmad Lahori. 22,000 workers and 1,000 elephants used in construction. Considered the finest example of Mughal architecture — a 'teardrop on the cheek of time' (Tagore).

QuestionText: Who is Sachin Tendulkar beyond cricket?
Options: A) Only a cricketer with no other contributions
B) Nominated Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha, 2012-2018), Bharat Ratna awardee, brand ambassador for various causes including health and children's welfare
C) A cricket coach after retirement
D) India's Minister of Sports
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Sachin Tendulkar (beyond cricket): Nominated to Rajya Sabha by President (2012-2018). Bharat Ratna (2014) — first sportsperson to receive India's highest civilian honour. UN Ambassador for rural development and nutrition. Adopted village Puttamraju Kandriga (Andhra Pradesh) under Saansad Adarsh Gram Yojana. Charity: Apnalaya (education), Shalaka Foundation (early learning). Knighted by Australia (honorary). ICC Cricket Hall of Fame. His retirement (2013) was marked by emotional farewell speeches — among the most watched cricket events ever in India. Continues to be cricket's global ambassador.

QuestionText: What is Holi and why is it celebrated?
Options: A) A festival marking India's Independence Day
B) Festival of Colours — celebrates arrival of spring and triumph of good over evil (Holika Dahan legend)
C) A harvest festival specific to Haryana
D) A festival marking Ram Navami
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Holi: Hindu spring festival (Phalgun/March). Two-day celebration: Night before: Holika Dahan (bonfire) — commemorates Prahlad's devotion and Holika's burning (evil demon Hiranyakashipu's sister who tried to kill devotee Prahlad — fire protected him). Main day: Rangwali Holi — people throw coloured powder and water on each other. Significance: arrival of spring, harvest season beginning, celebration of love (associated with Radha-Krishna). Celebrated joyfully across India and in Indian diaspora worldwide. Vrindavan and Mathura (UP): world's most famous Holi celebrations (Lath Mar Holi). Barsana, Nandgaon traditions are especially famous.

QuestionText: What is IPL (Indian Premier League)?
Options: A) Indian Parliamentary League for political debates
B) T20 cricket tournament started by BCCI in 2008 — world's most watched cricket league
C) India's professional football league
D) India's professional badminton league
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: IPL (Indian Premier League): Twenty20 franchise cricket tournament launched by BCCI in 2008. 10 teams representing Indian cities (Mumbai Indians, Chennai Super Kings, Kolkata Knight Riders, Royal Challengers Bengaluru, Rajasthan Royals, Sunrisers Hyderabad, Delhi Capitals, Lucknow Super Giants, Punjab Kings, Gujarat Titans). Annual April-May tournament. Broadcast to 200+ countries. Economic impact: ~$10+ billion annual economic value. Global players + Indian stars. Lalit Modi (first commissioner, 2008-2010) conceived the franchise model. IPL has changed cricket's economics globally. Mumbai Indians: most IPL titles (5). MS Dhoni: most successful IPL captain (CSK — 5 titles).

QuestionText: What are the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage elements from India?
Options: A) Taj Mahal, Ajanta Caves, Western Ghats
B) Yoga, Kumbh Mela, Navroze, Chhau dance, Vedic chanting — among 14+ Indian elements recognized
C) Bollywood, Ayurveda, Rajput architecture
D) Sanskrit literature, India cuisine, Kathak dance
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: UNESCO's List of Intangible Cultural Heritage includes Indian elements: Ramlila (dramatization of Ramayana), Vedic chanting, Kutiyattam (Sanskrit theatre, Kerala), Ramman (Garhwali festival), Mudiyettu (Kerala ritual), Kalbelia (Rajasthani dance), Chhau (martial dance), Sankirtana (Manipuri singing/drumming), Traditional brass/copper craft of Thatheras (Punjab), Yoga (2016), Nawrouz/Nowruz (shared with Iran), Kumbh Mela (2017), Durga Puja (Kolkata, 2021), Garba (Gujarat, 2023). India has one of the largest numbers of ICH elements globally, reflecting its extraordinary cultural diversity and depth.

QuestionText: Who is Sania Mirza in the context of Indian sports?
Options: A) India's national women's football captain
B) India's greatest women's tennis player — 6 Grand Slam titles (all in doubles/mixed), WTA World No.1 in doubles (2015)
C) India's top woman sprinter
D) A leading Indian chess player
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Sania Mirza: India's most successful women's tennis player. 6 Grand Slam titles (all doubles/mixed doubles): Australian Open (2009, 2015, 2016), French Open (2012, 2016), US Open (2014). Ranked World No. 1 in women's doubles (April 2015). Won doubles titles with various international partners (Martina Hingis, Cara Black). Broke Indian tennis's stereotypes of being male-dominated. Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, Arjuna Award, Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, Padma Vibhushan awardee. Retired from professional tennis (2023). Continues to inspire Indian women athletes. Born in Mumbai, trained in Hyderabad.

QuestionText: What is the significance of Indian cinema (Bollywood)?
Options: A) Bollywood makes fewer films than Hollywood
B) Mumbai's Hindi film industry is the world's largest film industry by number of films produced — a major part of India's soft power globally
C) Bollywood only appeals to Indian audiences
D) Indian cinema focuses entirely on classical art films
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Indian Cinema: India produces the most films annually (1,500-2,000 films per year) across multiple language industries — Bollywood (Hindi, Mumbai), Tollywood (Telugu, Hyderabad — globally successful with RRR, Baahubali), Kollywood (Tamil), Mollywood (Malayalam), Sandalwood (Kannada). Bollywood = Hindi film industry. Indian cinema has global audience: significant viewership in Middle East, Africa, South Asia, Russia, China (Aamir Khan's films). Dadasaheb Phalke Award: India's highest film honour. India's soft power: films, music, and cricket are major cultural ambassadors. RRR (Telugu, 2022): won Academy Award for Best Song ('Naatu Naatu').

QuestionText: What is the significance of Pandit Ravi Shankar?
Options: A) Famous Indian classical dancer
B) World-famous Indian sitar maestro who introduced Indian classical music to global audiences — collaborating with George Harrison and performing at Woodstock
C) India's leading poet in the independence era
D) A pioneer of Bollywood music composition
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Pandit Ravi Shankar (1920-2012): legendary Indian sitarist who became a global cultural ambassador for Indian music. Performed at Woodstock (1969), collaborated with Beatle George Harrison (who became his student), composed music for Satyajit Ray's Apu Trilogy films. Founded music schools in India and USA. Grammy Awards (4): first Indian musician to win. Bharat Ratna (1999). UN Medal of Peace. Introduced hundreds of millions of Westerners to Indian classical music. His daughter Anoushka Shankar continues his legacy. Norah Jones (born Geetali Norah Jones Shankar) is also his daughter — Grammy Award winning jazz/pop artist.

QuestionText: What is the Khelo India programme?
Options: A) A television game show about Indian sports
B) Government programme to revive India's sports culture at the grassroots level — discovering and nurturing sports talent
C) An international cricket league
D) An Olympic bid programme for India to host the Olympics
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Khelo India: Government of India scheme (under Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports) to revive India's sports culture at grassroots level. Components: Khelo India Youth Games (annual multi-sport event for school/college students), Khelo India University Games, annual scholarship for 1,000 talented athletes (₹5 lakh/year for 8 years). Also: upgrading sports infrastructure in schools and colleges, training coaches, identifying talent from rural areas. India's poor Olympic medal count (historically) led to such systematic talent identification programmes. Target Olympians 2028 (Los Angeles) and 2032 (Brisbane/India) programmes build on Khelo India.

QuestionText: What is Kathak dance?
Options: A) A classical dance form from Tamil Nadu
B) A classical dance form from North India — combining Hindu temple traditions and Mughal court influences
C) A folk dance from Punjab
D) A tribal dance from Northeast India
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Kathak: classical dance form from North India (Hindi-speaking belt — UP, Rajasthan, Delhi). Name from 'Katha' (story/narrative). Two schools (gharanas): Lucknow Gharana (Nawabi style — lyrical, graceful, Wajid Ali Shah patronised), Jaipur Gharana (vigorous footwork, vigorous tatkar). Distinctive elements: intricate footwork (tatkar — rhythmic stamping), spins (chakkar), expressive mime, abhinaya, wearing ghungroos (ankle bells). Major exponents: Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Kumudini Lakhia. Evolved from kathakars (storytellers in temples) — absorbed Persian/Mughal influences in Nawabi courts. One of India's 8 classical dance forms.

QuestionText: Who is Leander Paes?
Options: A) India's top badminton player
B) India's greatest men's tennis player — 8 Grand Slam doubles titles, 3 Olympic medals (best medal tally for any Indian in individual sports for years)
C) A legendary Indian table tennis champion
D) India's top squash player
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Leander Paes: India's greatest men's tennis player in doubles. 8 Grand Slam doubles titles (with various partners), Wimbledon Mixed Doubles champion, Davis Cup stalwart (India's record appearance holder). Olympic medal: Bronze in Singles at 1996 Atlanta Olympics — India's first individual Olympic medal (non-hockey) in 44 years. Received Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, Padma Vibhushan. Davis Cup record: won most matches for India. Partnered successfully with Mahesh Bhupathi, Martina Navratilova, Cara Black. Retired from professional tennis (2020). Inspired a generation of Indian doubles tennis players.

QuestionText: What is the National Film Awards of India?
Options: A) An Indian equivalent of the Golden Globes
B) India's premier film awards given by the Directorate of Film Festivals, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting — established 1953
C) Awards given by Bollywood's Film Producers' Guild
D) Annual awards voted by the public
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: National Film Awards (NFA): established 1954 (first ceremony). Presented annually by the President of India. Most prestigious: Dadasaheb Phalke Award (lifetime achievement — named after 'Father of Indian Cinema'), Best Film, Best Director, Best Actress, Best Actor, Best Regional Film. Not limited to Bollywood — recognises excellence across all Indian language films. Dadasaheb Phalke Award: Ritwik Ghatak, Raj Kapoor, Dilip Kumar, Hrishikesh Mukherjee, Lata Mangeshkar, Amitabh Bachchan, Waheeda Rehman (2023) are notable recipients. India's 'Oscars' — but judged by a government jury, not industry peers.

QuestionText: What is Carnatic music?
Options: A) Music from Karnataka only
B) South Indian classical music tradition — devotional, compositional, with elaborate ragas and talas — distinct from Hindustani tradition
C) North Indian classical music
D) Folk music from coastal Karnataka
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Carnatic music: South Indian classical tradition (Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala). Based on: Ragas (melodic scales/modes), Talas (rhythmic cycles), mainly vocal but rich instrumental tradition. Emphasis on compositions (kritis) — most famous: Thyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, Syama Sastri (Trinity of Carnatic music, 18th-19th century). Different from Hindustani: more composition-based, less improvisation, strong devotional orientation. M.S. Subbulakshmi: legendary Carnatic vocalist — first musician to receive Bharat Ratna. Instruments: veena (Saraswati veena), mridangam, violin, nadaswaram, ghatam. Sabhas (music organizations) in Chennai organize annual December Music Season.

QuestionText: What is Odissi dance?
Options: A) A folk dance from Odisha
B) A classical dance form from Odisha — among India's oldest surviving dance forms, characterized by tribhangi (three-part body bend)
C) A classical dance from Andhra Pradesh
D) A martial arts dance from Northeast India
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Odissi: classical dance from Odisha. Origin in temple dances of maharis (temple dancers) at Jagannath Temple, Puri. Characteristic tribhangi posture: three-part flexion of head, chest, and hip creating an S-curve. Expressive abhinaya depicting stories from Jayadeva's Gita Govinda (12th century Sanskrit poem on Radha-Krishna). Major exponents: Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra (revived it), Sanjukta Panigrahi, Protima Bedi, Sharon Lowen. Recognized by Sangeet Natak Akademi as classical dance form (1958). Sculptures of Odissi-like poses found in Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves (2nd century BCE) — evidence of its antiquity.

QuestionText: Who is Mary Kom?
Options: A) India's top woman table tennis player
B) 6-time World Amateur Boxing Champion and Olympic bronze medallist — from Manipur
C) India's leading woman sprinter
D) A classical dancer from Northeast India
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Mary Kom (Mangte Chungneijang Mary Kom): India's most decorated woman boxer. Achievements: 6-time World Amateur Boxing Champion (2002-2018), Olympic Bronze medalist (London 2012 — India's first boxing medal in Olympics for women), Asian Games gold medals, Commonwealth Games gold. Mother of three sons — continued competing after motherhood (inspiring story). From Kangathei village, Manipur. First became a world champion in 2002 at age 19. Padma Shri, Padma Vibhushan, Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna. Nominated to Rajya Sabha (2016). Her life story was depicted in the Bollywood film 'Mary Kom' (2014, Priyanka Chopra).

QuestionText: What are the Vedas?
Options: A) Ancient Indian legal codes
B) The oldest sacred scriptures of Hinduism — four collections of hymns, rituals, and philosophy (Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, Atharvaveda)
C) Ancient Sanskrit poems about kings
D) Buddhist religious texts
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Vedas: four oldest texts of Hinduism (1500-500 BCE). Rigveda: hymns to gods (oldest, most important). Samaveda: musical notations (origin of Indian classical music). Yajurveda: sacrificial rituals. Atharvaveda: spells, everyday life, medicine. 'Vedic period': 1500-500 BCE — early Indo-Aryan civilization in India. Vedic chanting: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (2008). Sanskrit (Vedic language): one of the world's oldest languages, mother of many Indian languages. Upanishads (philosophical texts) and Brahmanas (ritual texts) are associated literature. Vedas form the foundation of Hindu philosophy, ritual, and worldview.

QuestionText: Who is Amitabh Bachchan in Indian culture?
Options: A) India's leading classical musician
B) 'Megastar' of Indian cinema — 5-decade acting career, won 4 National Film Awards, Dadasaheb Phalke Award — cultural icon
C) India's most famous sports commentator
D) A legendary Indian chess player
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Amitabh Bachchan: the most iconic Bollywood star — acting career spanning 5+ decades since 1969. Known as the 'Big B' and 'Angry Young Man' (1970s). Famous films: Sholay, Deewar, Don, Mughal-E-Azam remastered (narrator), Mohabbatein, Pink, Gulabo Sitabo, Piku. 4 National Film Awards as Best Actor. Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan, Padma Vibhushan. Dadasaheb Phalke Award (2018). France's Légion d'Honneur (2007). Host of Kaun Banega Crorepati (Indian Who Wants to Be a Millionaire). His baritone voice is iconic. Health challenges (1982 liver injury, COVID-19 in 2020) did not diminish his stardom. Remains the most influential personality in Indian entertainment.

QuestionText: What is Garba dance and its cultural significance?
Options: A) A classical dance from Rajasthan
B) A traditional folk dance from Gujarat performed during Navratri — UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (2023)
C) A classical dance of Maharashtra
D) A temple dance from Tamil Nadu
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Garba: traditional folk dance from Gujarat, performed during Navratri (nine nights in honor of goddess Durga/Amba). Circular formations, clapping, movements around a central lit lamp or image of goddess. Dandiya Raas: played with colored sticks. UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (December 2023) — India's latest ICH inscription. Vadodara, Ahmedabad, Surat: famous for massive Garba events. Garba has become global — Indian diaspora celebrates it worldwide. Traditionally: religious and community-building; now: major cultural event and tourist attraction. Garba music: traditional folk to modern Bollywood-influenced styles.

QuestionText: What is Durga Puja and its cultural significance?
Options: A) A festival celebrated only in South India
B) A major Hindu festival honoring goddess Durga — most prominent in West Bengal, declared UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (2021)
C) A harvest festival specific to Assam
D) A festival marking the end of monsoon season
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Durga Puja: 10-day festival (Sharad Navaratri, September-October) celebrating Goddess Durga's victory over demon Mahishasura. Most celebrated in West Bengal (Kolkata) where it's a massive cultural extravaganza. Elaborately decorated pandals (temporary shrines) with artistic idol installations — compete for best pandal/idol. UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage (2021). Kolkata Durga Puja: millions of visitors, artisans from Kumartuli (pottery area), global media coverage. Also celebrated across India and globally in Indian diaspora communities. Visarjan (immersion): final day when idols are immersed in rivers/water bodies. Bengal's culture, arts, music, and cuisine are all on display.

QuestionText: What is the Ramayana and its cultural impact?
Options: A) An ancient Indian mathematics text
B) An ancient Indian epic (Valmiki) narrating Ram's life, his exile, Sita's abduction, and victory over Ravana — deeply embedded in Indian culture
C) A collection of Buddhist teachings
D) An ancient Indian law code
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Ramayana: one of India's two great epics (with Mahabharata). Written by Valmiki (7th-4th century BCE), ~24,000 verses. Story: Prince Ram of Ayodhya is exiled 14 years; wife Sita abducted by demon king Ravana of Lanka; Ram (with brother Lakshman and devotee Hanuman) defeats Ravana and rescues Sita. Cultural impact: enormous — celebrated through Ramlila (dramatic performances, UNESCO heritage), Diwali (marking Ram's return to Ayodhya), Dussehra (Ravana's defeat), Ram Navami. Regional versions: Valmiki Ramayana (Sanskrit), Ramcharitmanas (Tulsidas, Hindi), Kambaramayanam (Tamil), Krittibas Ramayana (Bengali). Forms of Ramayana found across Southeast Asia (indicating India's cultural influence).

QuestionText: Who is Mirabai Chanu in Indian sports?
Options: A) India's top woman shot putter
B) India's top woman weightlifter — won India's first medal at Tokyo 2020 Olympics (Silver in 49kg weightlifting)
C) A celebrated Indian archer
D) India's National Women's Football captain
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Mirabai Chanu (Saikhom Mirabai Chanu): India's star weightlifter from Manipur. Won Silver medal in 49kg weightlifting at Tokyo 2020 Olympics (July 24, 2021) — India's first medal at those Games, and India's first Olympic weightlifting medal since Karnam Malleswari's bronze at Sydney 2000. World Championship Gold (2017), Commonwealth Games Gold (2018 Gold Coast, 2022 Birmingham — world record). Khel Ratna, Padma Shri, Arjuna Award. India's sporting heroes often come from Northeast India — Manipur (Mary Kom, Mirabai Chanu) has produced exceptional sports talent despite limited resources.

QuestionText: What is the significance of the Mahabharata?
Options: A) An ancient Indian scientific text
B) The world's longest epic poem — contains the Bhagavad Gita, narrates the Kurukshetra War between Pandavas and Kauravas
C) A collection of ancient Indian laws
D) A history of the Mughal dynasty
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Mahabharata: attributed to Vyasa. World's longest epic (~100,000 verses — 3× longer than Homer's Iliad and Odyssey combined). Central story: conflict between Pandavas (five brothers including Arjuna) and Kauravas (hundred brothers led by Duryodhana) over kingdom of Hastinapur — leads to Kurukshetra War. Contains: Bhagavad Gita (Krishna's teachings to Arjuna about duty, dharma, moksha — one of Hinduism's most important texts), Shikhandi, Shakuntala, Nala-Damayanti stories. Cultural impact: television adaptation (B.R. Chopra, 1988-90) — one of India's most watched TV shows. Continuously influences Indian thought, ethics, law, philosophy, and culture.

QuestionText: What is the significance of R.K. Narayan in Indian literature?
Options: A) He wrote India's national anthem in English
B) One of India's greatest English-language novelists — created the fictional town of Malgudi depicting everyday Indian life
C) He wrote the Mahabharata in English
D) He was India's first Booker Prize winner
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: R.K. Narayan (Rasipuram Krishnaswami Iyer Narayanswami, 1906-2001): one of India's greatest English-language writers. Famous for fictional town of Malgudi (based on Mysore) — setting for novels including: Swami and Friends, The Bachelor of Arts, The English Teacher, The Guide (Sahitya Akademi Award, 1960 — adapted into Bollywood film), Malgudi Days (TV series by Shankar Nag). Malgudi captures small-town India's warmth, humor, and everyday life. Friend of Graham Greene (helped him publish). Padma Bhushan, Padma Vibhushan. India's other great English writers: Mulk Raj Anand, Raja Rao, Arundhati Roy (Booker Prize), Vikram Seth, Amitav Ghosh.

QuestionText: What is the Arjuna Award?
Options: A) India's highest military honour
B) India's second-highest sports honour — recognising outstanding achievement in sports over four years
C) The award given for the best individual performance in a single year
D) An academic award for sports science research
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Arjuna Award: established 1961, India's second-highest sports honour (after Khel Ratna/Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna). Named after legendary archer Arjuna from the Mahabharata. Criteria: outstanding performance over 4 years, sportsmanship, leadership. Cash prize: ₹15 lakhs + statuette. Given on National Sports Day (August 29 — Dhyan Chand's birthday). Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna: highest sports honour (previously Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna — renamed 2021). Dronacharya Award: for coaches (named after Arjuna's archery teacher Dronacharya). Dhyan Chand Award: lifetime achievement. India's sports awards system recognizes achievement from grassroots to international level.

QuestionText: What is the significance of cricket in Indian culture?
Options: A) Cricket is less popular than hockey in India
B) Cricket is India's de facto national sport — a cultural phenomenon binding the nation, with IPL making it the world's most economically powerful cricket league
C) Cricket only became popular in India after 1980
D) Cricket is primarily watched in cities, not rural areas
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Cricket in India: more than a sport — a national passion. History: introduced by British colonial rulers; India first played Test cricket 1932. India's proudest moments: 1983 World Cup (Kapil Dev's underdog team beat West Indies), 2011 World Cup (at home), Sachin Tendulkar's records. BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India): world's richest cricket board — controls ~70% of global cricket revenue. IPL: changed cricket economics globally. Every India vs Pakistan match is one of the world's most-watched sporting events (~1 billion viewers). Cricketers are treated as demigods — Sachin's retirement caused national grief. Cricket unites India across languages, regions, and religions.

QuestionText: What is the Bihu festival?
Options: A) A festival from Rajasthan
B) Assam's most important festival — three types (Bohag, Kati, Magh) marking agricultural seasons, celebrated with Bihu dance
C) A Buddhist festival from Sikkim
D) A harvest festival from Kerala
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Bihu: Assam's premier festival. Three types: Bohag/Rongali Bihu (April — spring, beginning of Assamese New Year, most celebrated), Kati/Kongali Bihu (October — sombre, paddy growing, lamps lit in fields), Magh/Bhogali Bihu (January — post-harvest, community feast). Bihu dance: folk dance by young men and women — energetic, colorful, accompanied by dhol, pepa (buffalo horn instrument), gagana. Traditional Bihu songs. Bohag Bihu: UNESCO is considering its recognition. Assam's cultural identity is deeply tied to Bihu. 'Rang Ghar' in Sivasagar: ancient royal sports stadium, venue for Bihu celebrations.

QuestionText: What is Manipuri dance?
Options: A) A folk dance from Manipur
B) One of India's 8 classical dance forms — from Manipur, graceful and devotional, depicting Radha-Krishna themes
C) A martial art from Northeast India
D) A tribal dance specific to Naga communities
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Manipuri: classical dance from Manipur, Northeast India. Unique characteristics: gentle, lyrical, circular movements — no sharp angles, graceful unlike most Indian classical forms; costumes include barrel-shaped skirt (potloi) for female dancers. Primarily depicts Vaishnavite devotion (Radha-Krishna themes), especially Ras Leela (five Ras Leelas from Raslila). Revived by Guru Bipin Singh, popularized by Rabindranath Tagore who incorporated it at Shantiniketan (Visva-Bharati University, 1919). One of 8 Sangeet Natak Akademi recognized classical forms. Unique musical instruments: pung (barrel drum), pena.

QuestionText: What is Pongal and its significance?
Options: A) A festival from Maharashtra
B) Tamil Nadu's harvest festival (January) — four-day celebration of sun, nature, cattle, and the rice harvest
C) A festival marking Tamil New Year
D) A festival specific to the fishing communities of Tamil Nadu
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Pongal: Tamil Nadu's most important harvest festival (mid-January — also observed in other South Indian states as Sankranti/Makara Vilakku). Four days: Bhogi (burning old possessions, welcoming new beginnings), Thai Pongal (main day — boiling newly harvested rice in earthen pots outdoors, letting it overflow as auspicious symbol, worshipping Sun), Mattu Pongal (honouring cattle), Kaanum Pongal (family outings). 'Pongal O Pongal' (overflow — symbol of abundance and prosperity). Kolam: intricate rice flour patterns in front of homes. Corresponds with Makar Sankranti (kite flying in Gujarat), Lohri (Punjab), Bihu (Assam) — all celebrating the sun's northward journey.

QuestionText: What is the significance of D. Gukesh in Indian sports?
Options: A) An Indian badminton prodigy
B) India's chess prodigy who became World Chess Champion in 2024 at age 18 — youngest ever to win the classical World Chess Championship
C) An Indian cricket star under 19
D) A junior Olympics gold medalist in swimming
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: D. Gukesh (Dommaraju Gukesh): chess prodigy from Chennai, Tamil Nadu. Became youngest-ever Classical World Chess Champion in December 2024 (age 18 years) — defeating reigning champion Ding Liren (China) in Singapore in a dramatic final game. Won the Candidates Tournament 2024 to earn the right to challenge Ding Liren. Part of India's extraordinary chess generation (along with Praggnanandhaa, Arjun Erigaisi, Nihal Sarin). India won Chess Olympiad 2024 gold in both Open and Women's categories. India's chess dominance is a remarkable story of systematic talent development, inspired by Viswanathan Anand's legacy.

QuestionText: What is Sattriya dance?
Options: A) A classical dance from Rajasthan
B) A classical dance form from Assam — developed by Srimanta Shankardev in the 15th-16th century in the Vaishnavite monasteries
C) A tribal dance from Meghalaya
D) A royal court dance from Manipur
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Sattriya: classical dance from Assam, developed by Srimanta Shankardev (15th-16th century) in the Satras (Vaishnavite monasteries). Recognized as India's 8th classical dance form by Sangeet Natak Akademi (2000). Traditionally performed only by male brahmacharya monks (bhokots) in the Satras for devotional purposes. Depicts episodes from Vishnu's life, Puranic stories. Choreographed by Shankardev himself. Unlike other classical forms: originated in a specific religious institution. Now performed publicly by male and female dancers. Traditional costumes: silk (Assam's famous Muga and Pat silk). Guwahati's Sattras are centers of this tradition.

QuestionText: Who was Dhyan Chand and why is his birthday celebrated as National Sports Day?
Options: A) India's first Olympic gold medalist in individual event
B) Legendary Indian hockey player called 'The Wizard' — scored 570+ international goals, led India to 3 Olympic gold medals (1928, 1932, 1936)
C) India's first cricket captain
D) India's legendary kabaddi player
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Major Dhyan Chand (August 29, 1905 – December 3, 1979): considered the greatest field hockey player of all time — 'The Wizard' of hockey. Scored 570+ goals in international career. Led India to Olympic gold (1928 Amsterdam — first Olympic gold, 1932 Los Angeles, 1936 Berlin — legend says Hitler offered German citizenship). 1936 Berlin Olympics: scored 6 goals in final; Hitler reportedly had his hockey stick broken to check if it had a magnet! National Sports Day: August 29 (his birthday). Khel Ratna renamed 'Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna' (2021). Dhyan Chand Award for lifetime achievement. Candidate for India's Bharat Ratna — widely considered overdue.

QuestionText: What is classical Indian sculpture?
Options: A) A modern art form developed post-independence
B) An ancient tradition spanning 2,500+ years — from Indus Valley to Gupta golden age to medieval temples (Khajuraho, Konark)
C) Sculptures imported from ancient Greece
D) A colonial-era art form introduced by the British
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Indian sculpture tradition: Indus Valley (2500 BCE) — Dancing Girl (bronze, Mohenjo-daro), Priest-King bust. Maurya period: polished sandstone Ashokan pillars, Lion Capital (now India's national emblem). Gupta period (4th-6th CE) — 'Golden Age' — refined naturalistic style, Buddhist/Hindu images (Sarnath Buddha). Khajuraho temples (10th-12th CE, MP): elaborately carved erotic sculptures — UNESCO World Heritage. Konark Sun Temple (Odisha, 13th CE): wheel-shaped, intricate sculptures — UNESCO World Heritage. Nataraja (Dancing Shiva — Chola bronze sculpture, Tamil Nadu): iconic image of Hindu cosmic dance. India's sculpture tradition influenced Southeast Asian art (Angkor Wat, Borobudur).

QuestionText: What is the significance of classical Indian literature?
Options: A) Most ancient Indian literature was written in English
B) Sanskrit literature is among the world's oldest and richest — Vedas, Mahabharata, Ramayana, Kalidasa's works — foundational to Indian culture and global literature
C) Ancient India produced no literary tradition
D) Indian literature began with the Mughal period
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Classical Indian literature: Sanskrit tradition spans 3,500+ years. Epics: Mahabharata, Ramayana (attributed to Vyasa and Valmiki). Kalidasa (5th century CE): India's greatest classical poet and playwright — Abhijnanasakuntalam (Shakuntala — story that inspired Goethe), Meghadutam, Kumarasambhavam, Raghuvamsham. Panchatantra: ancient Indian fables translated into 50+ languages (source for Aesop's Fables disputed). Arthashastra (Kautilya): statecraft treatise. Manusmriti: ancient law codes. Tamil classical literature: Sangam poetry (2,000+ years old) — Thirukkural (universal maxims). India's literary tradition is one of humanity's greatest cultural achievements.

QuestionText: What is the Onam festival?
Options: A) A festival from Tamil Nadu
B) Kerala's most important harvest festival — commemorating legendary King Mahabali's annual return, celebrated with Pookkalam, Onasadhya, Vallam Kali
C) A festival specific to Kerala's Christian community
D) A monsoon-welcoming festival of coastal Karnataka
Topic: General Knowledge - Sports, Arts and Culture
Explanation: Onam: Kerala's biggest festival (August-September, Chingam month). Commemorates the annual return of mythical King Mahabali (Maveli) — a beloved king whose soul visits Kerala during Onam. 10-day celebration: Pookkalam (intricate floral carpet designs — competing artistry), Onasadhya (grand feast of 26+ dishes on banana leaf — one of world's greatest food traditions), Vallam Kali (snake boat races — thrilling traditional rowing competitions), Pulikali (tiger dance), Kathakali performances, traditional games. Kerala Tourism markets Onam as a major tourist attraction. The festival uniquely represents Kerala's unity across Hindu, Muslim, and Christian communities.
